reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) from PMC10179711 directly supports the formation of a worm-like dual BCC structure with Cr addition, the associated improvement in room-temperature strength and ductility, and the mechanism of enhanced work-hardening and coordinated dual-phase deformation. However, the evidence comes from a different alloy system, not NbZrTiHfMo, so the transferability of the specific microstructural and mechanical effects to this new composition is assumed rather than demonstrated.
premises: Cr addition can induce a dual BCC (worm-like) microstructure in refractory high-entropy alloys
A dual BCC microstructure enhances room-temperature ductility while preserving high strength
Cr addition enhances work-hardening ability, which coordinates deformation and improves strain uniformity
The beneficial effect of Cr on strength-ductility balance is achieved through dual-phase coordinated deformation
